chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Asheym who said, Al-Rayyan ibn Shabeeb wrote to him, meaning Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him):

A man marries a woman by Mut'ah (temporary marriage) for a known term with a specified dower, and gives her part of her dower, and she delays him with the remainder. Then he consummates the marriage with her, and after consummation, before he pays her the remainder of her dower, he learns that she had married herself (to another) and has a husband residing with her. Is it permissible for him to withhold the remainder of her dower or is it not permissible?
So he (peace be upon him) wrote: 'He should not give her anything because she has disobeyed Allah, Mighty and Majestic.'
ai.seo_question: Can a husband withhold the remaining dower if his temporary wife has a living husband?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi clarifies the financial consequences in temporary marriage (Mut'ah) when a woman conceals her existing marital status, ruling that the husband retains the unpaid portion of the dower as compensation for her 'disobedience' (‘isyan). This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential view that the validity of the contract's core condition (freedom from impediments) directly impacts the financial settlement, distinguishing it from cases where the defect is discovered after full payment. The Imam’s verdict underscores the principle that the wife’s concealment of a major impediment voids her right to the remaining consideration.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Ahmad Bin Asheym who said, 
‘Al-Rayyan Bin Shabeeb wrote to him<sup>asws</sup>, meaning Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup>, ‘

The man married the woman by Mut’a to a known term, and gave her part of her dower, and delayed with the remainder. Then he slept with her, and came to know after having slept with her, before he had paid her the remainder of her dower, that she had married herself and there was a husband for her staying with her. Is it allowed for him that he withholds the remainder of her dower or is it not allowed?’
So he<sup>asws</sup> wrote: ‘He should not give her anything because she has disobeyed Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic’.
en.sarwar: Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn Ahmad ibn ‘Ushaym who has said the following: “Al-Rayyan ibn Shabib wrote to abu al-Hassan , ‘Alayhi al-Salam, asking about a man who marries in the manner of al-Mut‘ah (advantageous marriage) for a certain amount of mahr (dower) for a certain number of days, pays her a part of her mahr (dower) and withholds the rest, then he goes to bed with her and before paying her the rest, learns that she has a husband who lives with her, if it is permissible for him to withhold the remaining of her mahr (dower) or it is not permissible.
He (the Imam) wrote, ‘He must not give her anything because of her disobedience to Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious.’”
